newsitem.title: KENYA: Zairean city in government hands - aid groups.
newsitem.headline: Zairean city in government hands - aid groups.

text.p: The Zairean city of Kisangani remains in the hands of government forces, contrary to rebel claims that they control parts of it, aid organisations in east Africa said on Tuesday.
A Zairean rebel commander said on Monday that his forces had entered Kisangani, the largest city in eastern Zaire, and controlled some areas.

Commander John Kabunga, senior aide to rebel leader Laurent Kabila, told Reuters in the town of Goma that the rebels had reached Kisangani from the east by bypassing the intervening town of Walikale, where they had encountered difficulties.

The central government denied the report. "They are dreaming," government spokesman Boguo Makeli said in Kinshasa, capital of the central African country. "I deny categorically that they have taken the town."
"Kisangani was firmly in the hands of the government on Monday," one aid organisation official said in the eastern town of Goma. The organisation has an office in Kisangani.
"It can't be true. We sent a team to Kisangani yesterday and it was very normal at the airport," said one missionary source.
"They moved one tonne of medicines all the way from Kisangani to Lubutu and there was no sign of rebels," added the source. Lubutu is about halfway between Kisangani and Walikale.
"The rebels couldn't reach Kisangani without going through Lubutu," said the source.
The mission to Lubutu, 120 km (75 miles) southeast of Kisangani, found that about 15,000 Rwandan refugees and displaced Zaireans had recently arrived from the war zone.
"Many of them are weak, with 10 percent loss of body weight. They have come from the Goma/Bukavu area (on the Rwandan border) through Walikale," said the source.
